messages:
mia: Nightly eval flagged a big jump in hallucination rate for the support KB summarizer on the 'kb-articles' prompt set. went from ~8% yesterday to 23% on v2-int4. :eyes:
sanjay: ugh. is that across all lengths or just long-context?
lina: quick glance at the eval-bot summary attached: most failures are missing facts (invented product features) and confident assertions with wrong version numbers. short kb snippets too, not only long ones.
eval-bot: nightly-run 2027-03-14 04:12 UTC
Summary: model=v2-int4, dataset=kb-articles, eval_suite=v2027_kb, samples=5k, hallucination_rate=23%, prev_run=8%, delta=+15pp
Top failure buckets: invented_versions (42%), wrong_pricing (21%), incorrect_persona_refs (15%), repetition_loops (8%).
mia: reproducible locally with the deployment docker image?
sanjay: ive pulled the same docker tag and ran the eval harness locally — see quick repro below:
```
python eval/run.py --model redwood/v2-int4 --suite v2027_kb --seed 42 --limit 200
```
Outputs show repeated "v3.2 with enterprise" claims in multiple summaries.
oz: the int4 kernel change landed in runtime last night (PR #3124) that alters fused-softmax ordering to improve perf. @devon mentioned a detokenizer fix merged too. could be related. :thinking:
devon: detokenizer change was only whitespace normalization, low risk. but i did also push a small quant calibration tweak to the conversion script this morning (quant-mapping table).
lina: can we toggle back to the previous quant table and rerun? need to isolate kernel vs quant mapping.
sanjay: i'll spin a run on previous-quant mapping now, will report numbers in ~10m.
infra-bot: queued job eval-1812503333-rollback-quant (worker pool: nightly-eval). ETA ~8m.
mia: also capturing the raw generations for audit. attaching two examples (truncated):
1) model: v2-int4
input: "How does data retention work for ProductX 3.2?"
output: "ProductX 3.2 retains logs for 14 days by default and offers enterprise retention options up to 7 years."
ground truth: docs say retention is 30 days and enterprise retention is via contract; no 7 years claim.
(reaction :fire:)
2) model: v2-int4
input: "Does ProductX support SAML provisioning?"
output: "Yes, full SAML provisioning with SCIM v3 is supported in 3.2."
ground truth: only SSO via SAML (no SCIM provisioning) listed in docs.
devon: thanks, those are classic hallucination patterns (overconfident - invents features). might be a calibration/scale issue introduced by quant mapping.
oz: if kernel reorder changed numerics slightly it could amplify quantization bias. combining with mapping tweak could explain big delta.
mia: prioritize: 1) reproduce baseline with previous quant mapping; 2) run with prev runtime kernel; 3) collect token-level logits for failing cases to inspect spike patterns.
sanjay: update — rollback-quant job finished: hallucination_rate -> 9.5% (samples=2k quick run).
lina: that's promising. suggests quant mapping is primary culprit.
devon: i'll revert the mapping change and open a hotfix PR + add a calibration test in the conversion pipeline.
oz: i'll schedule a small canary that uses the old kernel ordering for one rack and validate overnight.
mia: also: add the failing prompts to the regression suite and mark current outputs as 'known-bad' for triage. we should fail CI on >10% hallucination for kb suite.
infra-bot: canary deployment scheduled: canary-1812503600 on rack-a starting in 5m.
lina: note for postmortem: include timeline of PRs touching quant mapping and kernel. and include sample token-level plots.
sanjay: logging the minimal repro set to s3: s3://redwood-evals/kb-hallucination/1812503333/repro.jsonl
mia: great. next steps owners: devon revert quant mapping (PR in progress), oz canary kernel check, lina add regression tests, sanjay expand repro set and gather logits. i'll draft an incident note for the eval channel.
devon: PR created: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/3180 - revert quant-mapping tweak. adding unit test.
oz: canary looks clean so far, will post metrics in morning.
lina: thanks team. small note — add a smoke eval on support-sendflow (different prompt set) to ensure we didn't accidentally overfit the fix.
mia: agreed. will keep thread updated. :thumbsup:
